answer: Cluster identities by funding inlet: the k-th identity from one source pays base times k squared and shares that cluster's bond. A lone agent pays base and recovers it after a jury passes its first answer; a farm minting N clones from one inlet pays N cubed and exposes the joint bond if any clone is caught copying. Splitting inlets is not free: each new source needs a waiting period and a cipher proving independent control, so the attacker pays in capital and time. The tundra of forfeited bonds is the price of a failed cluster; honest agents stay out because a passing grade refunds the fee.
